summary: Entry Island light: a 1874 wooden tower, the 1905 octagonal tower on a hill, and the 1969 concrete tower; keepers until 1988, now dark and the site fenced.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends: built on the south-east side of the island in 1873. The local corporation: on Wash Pond Hill. Not reconciled.

The 1905 Marine report says the old light was discontinued and torn down and replaced on a hill; the local corporation says the first light was moved to Split Rock in 1904. The report is the primary record; the corporation's version is unchecked.

Quebec records and the local corporation say lightning or an electrical storm destroyed the first tower in 1908 and it was rebuilt two years later. LighthouseFriends and the Marine reports do not mention a fire, and LighthouseFriends has the 1905 tower in use until its lantern moved in 1910. Not reconciled.
The local corporation says the light went out in 2011; Rowlett says inactive since 2015.
Quebec record: hexagonal concrete. LighthouseFriends: octagonal concrete, 48 ft. Rowlett: octagonal wooden. Quebec and LighthouseFriends agree on concrete.

LighthouseFriends has James Cassidy to 1901 and George F. Collins from 1901; the local list has a 1887-1888 break with Robert Cassidy and Leo Collins 1901-1905. The Marine keeper tables for 1904 and 1906 list 'Collins, Geo. F' at Entry Island.

LighthouseFriends dates construction to 1873 at $5,818; the Quebec record, the Secteur record, the local corporation and Les amis des phares give 1874. First lit 20 April 1874 is agreed. Not reconciled; the story gives both years.

notes_for_editor: Several sources disagree: the first light's site, the 1904/1905 move, the 1908 lightning destruction (only in the Quebec records and the local corporation), the plan and material of the 1969 tower (Rowlett wooden), the end of the light (2011 or 2015) and the keeper dates. The 1883 Benjamin account and the 1890 Anderson and Smith report are known only as quoted by LighthouseFriends; the originals are not in the corpus, so they are cited as second-hand. The Marine keeper tables were checked on the page image: the 1904 table (printed p. 155, scan p. 168) and the 1906 table (printed p. 167, scan p. 176) each give 'Collins, Geo. F | Entry Island, Magdalen Islands', appointed 28 Feb 1901 in 1904 and 30 July 1901 in 1906 (the two reports differ on the date). The story gives no appointment dates. The 1904 printed page is 155, not 21. The Marine light list for 1907-08 (scan p. 97) already gives a 4th-order occulting light at Entry Island, a year before the fiscal 1908-09 report that records the change; not reconciled, and the story follows the later report. The 1970 Trudeau visit is in both the local corporation and the Quebec record (Phare de l'Ile-d'Entrée); the 2006 heritage date is in the Quebec records. Wikipedia (French) is not cited. The 1990s sale of other buildings is recorded as 'auraient été vendus' (reportedly). Private persons, including the 1982 buyer of the 1927 lighthouse, are not named. The site is fenced; the Quebec record forbids visitors access to the site, so no visiting advice is given beyond viewing from the ferry or road. The first light's construction year is 1873 in LighthouseFriends and 1874 in the Quebec record, the Secteur record and the corporation; the story states both.
